subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: For Windows exec commands containing PowerShell expansion tokens, should OpenClaw support them through explicit one-shot approval, or document them as unsupported and require script-file/direct patterns?
rationale: Current source rejects these tokens for approval analysis, while supporting them changes the command-execution approval boundary and needs maintainer intent plus real Windows/Gateway proof.

options.title: Support via one-shot approval
options.body: Require the linked PR or equivalent to prove `$...` PowerShell payloads reach explicit one-shot approval and cannot become reusable or auto-reviewed trust.

options.title: Document as unsupported
options.body: Close the implementation path and document that Windows exec `$...` PowerShell payloads should be run through script files or other direct patterns instead of inline exec commands.

options.title: Redesign Windows exec contract
options.body: Pause the PR and define a broader Windows shell invocation/quoting contract before changing approval behavior.

recommendation.title: Support via one-shot approval
recommendation.body: Require the linked PR or equivalent to prove `$...` PowerShell payloads reach explicit one-shot approval and cannot become reusable or auto-reviewed trust.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across exec approval boundary work and is a good owner for the product/security contract choice.
